description: yo, gonna go alone and win it
summary: EmberWatch harmonises two decades of satellite fire detections into a single, comparable record. MODIS and VIIRS cannot be compared directly: they have different resolutions, sensitivities and overpass schedules, so plotting the raw feeds makes it look like burning jumped over 400% in 2012 when only the instrument changed. EmberWatch fixes this by counting “cell-days” instead of raw detections, applying a shared sensitivity floor, and calibrating the sensors against each other over their overlap years. The result is one burning-activity calendar spanning 2000 to today for any area on Earth. Draw a box on the map and it recomputes the calendar, flags whether the current month is normal or extreme against 25 years of history, and runs a seasonal Mann-Kendall trend test, all live in the browser. Crucially, the method grades itself: the artificial jump at the sensor change falls from +446% to +12%, measured and shown. It gives fire managers the consistent baseline they currently lack.
details: EmberWatch is a static web application backed by a Python data pipeline. The pipeline (DuckDB + Python) normalises MODIS and VIIRS FIRMS detections into one schema, bins them to a 0.25-degree grid, reduces them to cell-days to remove pixel-size and platform-count bias, clips both sensors to a shared fire-radiative-power floor, and fits per-cell calibration ratios over the sensor overlap. The front end is a single self-contained HTML page: a drawable world map, a 25-year calendar heatmap, a live seam test, percentile anomaly readouts and a seasonal Mann-Kendall trend test, all recomputed in-browser from a sparse per-cell export, so there is no backend to fail. Tools: Python, DuckDB, NumPy, vanilla JavaScript and SVG, Natural Earth coastlines. The creative core is treating two satellites like two mismatched log sources and applying detection-engineering discipline: normalise, baseline, alert on deviation. The project validates itself by measuring the residual seam (down to +12% from over +400%) rather than asserting the method works. A single-hue, colour-vision-safe palette and honest, stated limitations round it out.
